title: Examen de nivel C1
description: Demuestra que tienes el nivel C1 del Marco Común Europeo (MCER): gramática, vocabulario, comprensión lectora y comprensión auditiva.

syllabus.label: Cleft sentences (What I need is…, It was… who…)
Inversión tras expresiones negativas (Never have I…, Little did I know…)
Participle clauses (Having finished…, Built in 1890…)
Phrasal verbs avanzados y separables (turn down, come up with, talk into)
Hedging: It would appear that…, there seems to be…, tend to
Modales en pasado: needn't have, must / can't / might have, should have
would rather, had better
Condicionales sin if: provided that, unless, but for, should you…
Nominalización y registro formal
Marcadores: nevertheless, admittedly, that said, mind you
Énfasis: do / did, such / so, anteposición
Futuro en el pasado: was going to, was about to, would, was supposed to
Elipsis y sustitución (I hope so, I'd love to, So would I)
Probabilidad: bound to, likely to, due to, set to
Tiempos narrativos: had been doing, would, used to
La pasiva en todas sus formas (having been told, might have been lost)
Condicionales mixtos, wish e if only (repaso de B2)
Futuros: future continuous y future perfect (repaso de B1–B2)
Falsos amigos (actually, eventually, sensible, embarrassed)
Lenguaje aproximativo (or so, -ish, sort of, and stuff)
Expresiones idiomáticas
Vocabulario de empresa y finanzas
Registro formal e informal

variants.title: The village that turned off the lights
variants.text:
Twenty years ago, the small Welsh village of Llanfair was struggling. The quarry had closed, young people had been leaving for years, and the local school was about to shut its doors. Then a retired astronomer suggested something that most residents found absurd: switching off the street lights.

"People thought I'd lost my mind," Dr Ann Pryce remembers. "They had been asking the council for more lights, not fewer." Eventually, after months of argument, the village agreed to a six-month trial.

What happened next took everyone by surprise. Within a year, Llanfair had been officially recognised as a Dark Sky Reserve, and stargazers began arriving from all over Europe. Two guest houses opened, followed by a café and a small observatory, which was paid for entirely by local donations.

"If we hadn't taken that risk, the village wouldn't exist in its current form," says the mayor, Huw Davies. "I sometimes wish we'd done it ten years earlier."

Not everyone is convinced. Some older residents complain that the lanes are dangerous at night, and the council has been asked to install low-level lighting on the main road. Nevertheless, the numbers are hard to argue with: visitor spending is expected to reach two million pounds this year, and by 2030 the observatory will have welcomed half a million visitors.

Dr Pryce, now eighty-one, is modest about her role. "I didn't save Llanfair. The sky did. I just reminded people to look up."

options: They had been asking for more lights, not fewer.
They had never been interested in the stars.
The council had just installed new lights.

options: With money given by local people.

options: Half a million people will have visited the observatory.

variants.title: The café where everyone talks
variants.text:
When Sofia Marín opened a small café in Leeds in 2015, she had been working as a translator for a decade and was, in her own words, "bored of talking to computers". Her idea was simple: customers who spoke at least two languages would get a discount, provided they agreed to chat with learners for half an hour.

At first, the concept was dismissed as a gimmick. "A local critic wrote that we'd be closed within six months," Sofia laughs. "Actually, I think his review is what saved us. Suddenly everyone wanted to see the café he hated."

Today the café hosts conversation tables in fourteen languages, and similar cafés have been set up in Manchester, Glasgow and Dublin. A study carried out by a local university found that learners who attended regularly became far more confident speakers than those who only took classes.

"If I'd listened to the critics, I'd still be translating washing-machine manuals," Sofia says. "My only regret is that I didn't open a bigger place. We have to turn people away every Friday."

The future looks bright. A fifth café is due to open in Bristol in the spring, and by the end of next year the network will have trained more than two hundred volunteer hosts. Sofia, however, is in no hurry. "Growth is lovely," she says, "but a café is bound to lose its soul if it grows too fast."

dialogue.speaker: Priya
dialogue.text: So, the wedding. My mum's invited three hundred people or so.

dialogue.speaker: Lucía
dialogue.text: Three hundred! I thought you were going to keep it small.

dialogue.speaker: Priya
dialogue.text: I was going to, but you know my mum. She does love a party.

dialogue.speaker: Lucía
dialogue.text: Would you rather have a small wedding?

dialogue.speaker: Priya
dialogue.text: Honestly? I'd rather we ran away to Cornwall. But I can't do that to her.

dialogue.speaker: Lucía
dialogue.text: Do you need any help with the planning?

dialogue.speaker: Priya
dialogue.text: I'd love some. Could you design the invitations?

dialogue.speaker: Lucía
dialogue.text: Of course I will. When do they have to be ready?

dialogue.speaker: Priya
dialogue.text: By the end of the month-ish. And you'd better not make them too fancy, or Mum will want gold.

dialogue.speaker: Lucía
dialogue.text: Gold invitations? Over my dead body.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The tour was meant to finish in June, but they've added ten more dates.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel

dialogue.text: I am. Mind you, I was about to book a holiday. Two weeks in Greece or something.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Would you rather cancel the extra dates?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: No way. Such a chance doesn't come twice. I'd rather put the holiday off.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Will you come back to Bristol between concerts?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I hope so. I want to see how Priya's wedding plans are going. She'll kill me if I don't.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: She would. You'd better be there for the wedding, at least.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I will. Wild horses couldn't stop me.
